# Subscription unit economics
**All figures are projections from stated assumptions, not actual revenue.** Generated by `python3 scripts/unit-economics.py` — change the inputs there and re-run.

## Assumptions
- Prices: Free $0, Standard $12, Premium $24 per month (USD).
- HandyPay fee 4.9% + $0.40 per charge (documented); payout/FX fees unknown and excluded.
- Variable cost per user/month: Free $0.01, Standard $0.02, Premium $0.03 (estimates, see FEATURE_DELIVERY_COSTS).
- Fixed: $46/mo to 600 users; +Resend $20 beyond; +Vercel/DB/Sentry ~$71 beyond 1,000 users (estimates).
- "Registered users" scenarios use example tier mixes (Free/Standard/Premium). Typical freemium SaaS converts low single-digit % of free users; **nobody has paid yet**, so these mixes are illustrations.
- Excluded: founder time, legal review, advertising, taxes, refunds, chargebacks, founding-member discounts.

Blended contribution per payer (70/30): $14.41. Break-even at launch fixed cost $46/mo: 3.2 payers.

## Reading this
- Each paying subscriber contributes ~92%+ after fees; the product has almost no marginal cost. **The business risk is acquisition and conversion, not delivery cost.**
- Break-even on platform costs is ~3–4 paying subscribers; covering legal/DPA one-offs (~$400–1,800) needs a few months at that level.
- Ads change this: a $50 test that yields 1 paying Standard user is a $50 CAC against ~$11/month contribution → ~5-month payback if they stay.
- Premium mainly helps if it gets real Premium-only features; today most payers will rationally pick Standard.
